newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Jon Fox claims Pennsylvania election victory.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Jon Fox claims Pennsylvania election victory.

text.p: Republican U.S. Representative Jon Fox claimed re-election victory by fewer than 100 votes Wednesday, saying an official tablulation confirmed results last week declaring him the winner.
"This is a victory speech, and you can call me 'Landslide Fox,'" the freshman congressman quipped at a news conference after the count was completed.

Fox held a 10-vote lead over his Democratic challenger, County Commissioner Joseph Hoeffel going into the official tabulation of results from the Nov. 5 election. The tabulation, finished Wednesday, showed his lead increasing to more than 80 votes, Fox said.

"We heard from our people that the numbers were somewhere in the high 80s, so we feel very good that the election night count and the count today mirror each other," Fox told Philadelphia television station WPVI.
Officials of the Montgomery County Board of Elections said the tabulation was still being entered into computers and might not be certified and released until Friday.
Hoeffel could not immediately be reached for comment. Local media said his campaign aides had not yet conceded.

Fox, representing the predominantly Republican 13th Congresssional District in prosperous Montgomery County in suburban Philadelphia, had been targeted by the national Democratic Party and the AFL-CIO trade union federation, which ran a heavy advertising campaign against him.

Fox in his campaign played down his 1994 signing of Newt Gingrich's "Contract With America" and cast himself as an independent-minded Republican, stressing his service to constituents and such achievements as deficit reduction.
President Clinton easily carried the district.

"We were still able to prevail," Fox said Wednesday. "In almost every district where there was so much money by outside special interests spending funds against the freshmen ... when President Clinton won by a margin like this, they lost."
